info.name: SmartLogistics
info.description:
Auto-generated from every service's OpenAPI schema by `scripts/generate_api_docs.py` (`./dev.sh docs`). Do not edit by hand.

All requests go through the gateway (`base_url`, port 8000).

request.description: Every service fetches this once and verifies tokens locally.

item.name: Authenticate and receive a token pair

request.description:
The access token carries role, warehouse scope and courier id, so every
other service can authorise without calling Identity.

item.name: Exchange a refresh token for a new pair

request.description: Refresh tokens rotate. Replaying a rotated token revokes every session.

item.name: Service account: exchange client credentials for a system token

request.description:
For services acting on their own behalf (the orchestrator dispatching a
shipment), not for people. The token has role `system`, lives a few
minutes and has no refresh token: the caller asks again.

header.description: Send a unique value to make retries safe.

item.name: Warehouses an operator is scoped to
Scope an operator to a warehouse

request.description:
The warehouse id is checked with the Warehouse service — there is no
foreign key across databases. The operator's sessions are revoked so their
next token carries the new scope.

Address, coordinates, entrance, geofence, phone and hours of active
facilities — nothing about capacity, contacts or layout.
Operators see only the warehouses in their token's scope.

header.description: Send a unique value to make retries safe.

request.description:
Only `active` facilities may originate shipments. Shipment and Inventory
learn about the change from the `warehouse.status_changed` event.
Operators see only their warehouses. `available_qty` is a generated column.
Every change leaves a ledger entry. A result below the held quantity is refused.

Operators can only sweep their own warehouses — a `warehouse_id` outside
their scope is refused (the monolith let it through).

item.name: Hold stock for a shipment (all lines or none)

request.description:
Rows are locked in id order, so concurrent requests for the same units
serialise: the first wins and the second gets `insufficient_stock`. The
hold stays *unconfirmed* until `shipment.created` arrives, and returns the
SKU facts Shipment snapshots onto its items.

item.name: Confirm a hold (normally driven by shipment.created)
Create a shipment and hold its stock

header.description: Send a unique value to make retries safe.

request.description:
Reserves stock with Inventory first (one synchronous call), then records
the shipment and `shipment.created` in one transaction. With an
`Idempotency-Key`, a retry returns the original response and reuses the
same hold.

Row-scoped: operators see their warehouses, couriers their assignments.
Served entirely from this service's database — no calls to other services.

item.name: Move a shipment to the next state

request.description:
Validated against the state machine; every transition writes an audit
row and a `shipment.status_changed` event. Concurrent changes to the same
shipment cannot both apply: the loser gets 409 `concurrent_update`.

item.name: Dispatch a shipment (starts the dispatch workflow)

request.description:
Accepted, not done: the shipment moves to `dispatching` and the dispatch
workflow takes over — validate, confirm stock, print labels, assign a
courier, start tracking — then records `dispatched`, or `dispatch_failed`
with the reason (after undoing what it did). Follow it on this shipment's
status, or in the Temporal UI under `dispatch_workflow_id`. Retry a failed
dispatch by moving it back to `ready_for_dispatch`.

One A6 PDF per package with a Code 128 barcode. Called by the dispatch
workflow (an admin may re-print); safe to repeat.
Inventory releases the hold when it receives the status event.

`user_id` links the profile to the partner's login; Identity mirrors the
link from the `courier.created` event, so their token carries `courier_id`.

item.name: Go on shift, take a break or go offline

request.description:
Only `available` couriers receive new automatic assignments. Going offline
keeps the shipments already carried.

Suspending also takes the courier offline; shipments they carry stay with
them until reassigned.

item.name: Set a courier's availability on their behalf
Assign a courier to a shipment (automatic or chosen)

request.description:
Called by the dispatch workflow. Without `courier_id` the best courier is
chosen: same city as the warehouse, available, below capacity, based at
this warehouse first, then least loaded. Candidates are locked with
`SKIP LOCKED`, so concurrent dispatches never double-book a courier.
Repeating the call for the same shipment returns the same assignment.

item.name: Hand a shipment to another courier (manual override)

request.description:
Releases the current assignment and starts a new one, in one transaction.
Without `courier_id` the best *other* courier is chosen. Publishes
`courier.unassigned` then `courier.assigned`; Shipment follows.
A no-op (returns null) when nothing is assigned, so compensation can retry.

`workflow_id` is the shipment's `dispatch_workflow_id`
(`dispatch-<shipment>-<attempt>`). Shows the current step while running and
the outcome once finished; the Temporal UI (:8233) has the full history.

item.name: A shipment's journey with its timeline

request.description:
Pickup, progress, delivery attempts, location. Safe to retry: the same
`event_id` is recorded once and comes back as `duplicate`. Milestones reach
the shipment through the delivery workflow, which validates them.

item.name: Report many field updates at once (offline sync)

request.description:
For a device coming back online: each update is processed on its own and
gets its own result, in occurred order; duplicates and rejections never
fail the batch.

What a customer sees with their tracking number: milestones and times,
never the courier's identity or position.
